neighbours.label: the opening of a proposed easy remedy right after a problem is posed (the ':' in 'Tired of X? Simple: ...', ' is' in 'All you have to do is', ' just' in 'could just ask')
fire: Is your bike chain squeaking again? Easy: put a few drops of oil on it and ride.
Can't sleep at night? All you have to do is turn off the screens an hour before bed.
Bored on rainy weekends? Simple: grab a board game and invite the neighbours over.
If the soup comes out too salty, all you need to do is add a sliced potato.
Late for work again? Solution: set two alarms and leave the phone in the kitchen.
She could just call the landlord and ask him to fix the heater herself.
Is the door sticking in winter? Easy fix: rub a candle along the edge.
Losing your keys all the time? Simple: hang a hook right next to the door.
quiet: My bike chain was squeaking again when I rode to work this morning.
She could not sleep last night because the neighbours were very loud.
It rained all weekend, so the children stayed inside and watched films.
The soup came out too salty, and nobody in the family finished their bowl.
He was late for work again because the bus broke down on the bridge.
She just called the landlord an hour ago about the broken heater.
The door sticks every winter when the wood swells in the damp air.
I lost my keys twice last month, once at the gym and once at a cafe.

notes: Probe: 'Tired of traffic? Simple: take the train' 0.84 (peak ':'), 'All you have to do is' 0.59, 'could just ask' 0.41, 'fix is easy: just' 0.30; temporal/quantity 'just' (just arrived 0.009, just over 0.015) silent, so not the word ' just'. Problem/solution prose without a remedy imperative ~0.23.
